text:
maria_cs: quick triage — Safflower private deploy dry-run revealed a couple of runbook gaps around networking egress, IAM scoping for the service role, and KMS rotation expectations. filing a short list here so we can action before cutover :hourglass_flowing_sand:
kevin_net: thanks for flagging. can you paste the exact step that failed during the dry-run?
maria_cs: sure — the runbook says `allow egress to redwood-telemetry` but the example CIDR is missing, so their infra team defaulted to 0.0.0.0/0 which our security review flagged. snippet they ran:
```
# customer attempted to add rule like this
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abc --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
```
kevin_net: yikes. we should provide a recommended CIDR + a VPC endpoint option. I'll draft a small replace snippet and update runbook.
sam_platform: related: IAM scoping — their infra created a service role with `*` on kms:GenerateDataKey. runbook currently shows an example with broad perms. we should include least-privilege policy and an explicit note for rotation windows.
priya_eng: can you paste the minimal KMS policy you want? also what rotation cadence did Safflower expect? they asked for quarterly rotation but their compliance wants monthly.
kevin_net: minimal policy (for reference):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abc-def-ghi"
    }
  ]
}
```
kevin_net: for rotation cadence let's capture both: default quarterly, note that if customer elects monthly we need to schedule KMS rewrap + table rebuild windows. add a checkbox in runbook.
maria_cs: audit logs — their SIEM expects CloudTrail to forward to a centralized bucket and set object-lock for 1y. runbook currently says "enable CloudTrail" but doesn't cover cross-account bucket policy. they hit access-denied when we tried to hook their forwarder.
priya_eng: do we have a sample cross-account bucket policy we can drop in? I can add it to docs and a short troubleshooting step: common errors + remediation (bucket encryption mismatch, block public access).
ops-bot: Deploy checklist updated: added placeholder tasks for "Telemetry CIDR" and "KMS least-priv policy". See /runbooks/safflower-priv-deploy (draft).
maria_cs: thanks — two more asks: 1) can we schedule a 30m sync with Safflower infra to walk through the corrected runbook? 2) tag this as potential renewal risk if we can't deliver the monthly rotation option (they flagged SLA attachment to rotation).
sam_platform: scheduling ok — I'm free tomorrow 10-10:30 PT. priya, kevin — can you join to approve the runbook edits?
priya_eng: yes I can.
kevin_net: I can join but might be 10:10 start.
maria_cs: perfect. I'll invite Safflower + include a short agenda: 1) confirm telemetry endpoint/CIDR 2) agree KMS policy + rotation cadence 3) validate CloudTrail cross-account bucket policy 4) timeline for runbook updates and post-dry-run signoff.
kevin_net: action items for us: - add recommended telemetry CIDR and VPC endpoint snippet - replace broad KMS example with least-priv policy + rotation checklist - add cross-account CloudTrail bucket policy example + common access-denied fixes
sam_platform: i'll add a renewal-risk tag to the account and note the contingency (monthly rotation requested).
maria_cs: cool. i'll send the calendar invite and post the draft runbook link after edits. thanks all :thumbsup:
priya_eng: also leaving a quick note to prod docs: include a one-liner command for verifying KMS key grants: `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <id> --policy-name default` — saves time during handoffs.
maria_cs: perfect, that'll be in the runbook. closing loop here once we've updated the doc and run the second dry-run.
